name: Merricks Beach
intro: Merricks Beach is a hamlet, not a town, and is largely the work of one generation of holiday-house builders who put up timber shacks along the dunes in the 1950s and 60s and then refused to let the place change much since. The beach is shallow, tide-dependent, and quiet  -  there is no surf, no foreshore café strip, and at low tide it spreads out into hundreds of metres of flat sand that visiting children turn into a private kingdom. The Merricks General Store, technically up in Merricks village, is the one polished thing nearby and is famous for a reason. Stay at Merricks Beach if you want the holiday-house feeling the Peninsula has mostly lost: front-door dunes, no shops, neighbours you have to walk past, and an evening rhythm built around a sundowner on the verandah.
factualLede: Merricks Beach is a small residential hamlet on the Mornington Peninsula's Western Port coast, 80 km from Melbourne, with a shallow tide-dependent beach and no commercial centre.

heroImage.alt: Shallow Western Port tide flats at Merricks Beach with timber holiday houses set behind the dunes

tldr: Merricks Beach is a 1950s-built holiday-house hamlet on a shallow Western Port beach — quiet, low-rise, no shops.
Best for: families with small children; couples wanting a slow weekend; anyone who values the old holiday-house Peninsula feeling.
Signature experience: low-tide afternoon on the sand flats, sundowner on the verandah, dinner from Merricks General Store the next day.
Two nights minimum; mid-week off-season is the best version.
There is no shop — pre-buy in Balnarring or Merricks village.
signature: A 1950s holiday-house hamlet with a tide-flat beach and no commercial centre — the Peninsula's quietest piece of coast.
skip: Looking for a town to wander — Merricks Beach is a residential hamlet, by design.
bestDay: Late breakfast at Merricks General Store up in the village, drive back down for a low-tide walk along the sand flats, swim when the tide returns, sundowner on the verandah.
insiderNote: Check tides before booking — at low tide the water is a long walk away; at high tide it's at the dunes. Both have their pleasures, but only one suits children.
